known_before_this_freeze: The rule was designed after three ledgered runs on spent pilot seeds only (the 60 unmodified episodes of the m3-protocol-1, -2 and -3 pilots, 10900 to 10919, 10300 to 10319 and 10920 to 10939, each rebuilt as its run built it): 20261108T044149Z_1a94815d (goal_diagnostic, clean 98603c4), 20261108T044845Z_616d515d (goal_rule_diagnostic, clean 15f393f) and 20261108T045902Z_f0336752 (goal_envelope_analysis, clean d8b15c1, computed from the second run's records, no simulation). In-sample findings: (a) seed 10936 frame 114 showed 13 green pixels, 2.9% of the goal's projected disc (w = 0.029): the gripper covered the goal; and the snapshot render's own goal there was about half hidden (w = 0.51), which moved protocol-3's reference centroid 5.2 px from the projected centre; 4 of 60 snapshot renders had a partly hidden goal. (b) The candidate rule 'check frames with at least 90% of the snapshot's green count' does not separate: its widened tolerance, 11.02 px, is 0.34 px under the smallest 3 cm shift; a 3 cm shift could pass in 165 eligible frames; 11 of 60 final frames are ineligible. (c) 90% of the goal's projected area instead of the snapshot's count does separate in eligible frames (largest normal drift 1.75 px; a shift leaves at least 11.63 px), but 13 of 60 final frames are ineligible and on average 13.7% of type-4 injection steps have no eligible frame after them. (d) For a fully visible goal the green count is the projected disc's area (fill fraction median 1.003, 0.958 to 1.031 over the 56 scenes whose snapshot goal is not hidden). (e) The envelope holds in every one of the 10,121 frames with green, the largest excess of centroid distance over rho(w) r being 0.89 px. (f) Every final frame has w >= 0.452 (10912; next 0.500). (g) With the 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor, no unmodified episode fails, and none of 3,729,600 computed 0.03 m goal-pixel shifts (every step 1 to T - 1, every direction every 1 degree, every episode) passes; at every final frame the shift lands at least 2.55 px beyond the envelope (1.05 px beyond the margin). (h) A 0.03 m shift leaves the envelope, for every direction, in every frame with w >= 0.5, in 401 of 406 frames with 0.4 <= w < 0.5, and in 255 of 364 with 0.3 <= w < 0.4. The 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor were chosen from these numbers; every count is in-sample.

ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t; and (iii), for frame eligibility only, the joint positions and cube position that restore_state of the scene's saved initial state returns, the human render camera's centre (the translation column of the snapshot manifest's cam2world_gl), and the candidate's actions a_1 to a_T, a_t being the absolute pd_joint_pos target applied at control step t. An injection alters frames and the manifest, never (iii). No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.size_checkable_frames: The sightline is the segment from the camera's centre to the cube's initial centre. The arm's skeleton at a joint vector is arm_segments in the pinned src/vishwaroop/sim/so100_kinematics.py: line segments, without the links' thickness, from the base (world position (-0.725, 0, 0), yaw pi/2) through each joint origin of the mani_skill 3.0.1 SO-100 URDF chain in order to the fixed jaw's frame, then to the fixed jaw tip, and through the moving jaw's origin to its tip. Its clearance is the shortest distance from any skeleton segment to the sightline. Frame 0 is size-checkable when the clearance at the initial joint positions is more than 0.035 m; frame t >= 1 when frame t - 1 is and the clearance at a_t (all six values) is more than 0.035 m. So the size-checkable frames are frames 0 to n - 1, n between 0 and T + 1: the frames before the arm is first commanded near the sightline. The clearance is tested at the commanded targets only, not at the rendered arm, which lags them. Because the sightline ends at the cube's centre, a clearance above 0.035 m also keeps every skeleton segment more than 0.035 m from that centre. Both are geometric proxies; the pilot checks their premise in the simulator (stops 2 and 3). No image, mask or cube-area measurement enters this rule, so a resized, removed or duplicated cube cannot change which frames are size-checkable.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule in evals/M3-exit-tests.json
ET-M3-1.visibility: For a frame, r is its merged red area (the red components whose centroids lie within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid, under this protocol's pilot-set merge radius) divided by the snapshot render's merged cube area, compared unrounded. A frame shows the cube when r >= 0.02; shows no cube when r = 0; and its visibility is uncertain when 0 < r < 0.02. 0.02 is about 12 pixels of a cube of about 600 at 512 x 512. It is fixed here, not set by a pilot.
ET-M3-1.goal_geometry: From the snapshot manifest only, never from a frame or the candidate manifest: p, the goal's projected centre, is the snapshot manifest's goal_position under intrinsic_cv @ extrinsic_cv (row v / w, column u / w); d is the camera-to-goal distance, the norm of extrinsic_cv @ (goal_position, 1); r = f_x tan(asin(R / d)) px with f_x = intrinsic_cv[0][0] and R = 0.015625 m, the goal sphere's radius (mani_skill 3.0.1 PickCube 'so100' goal_thresh, 0.0125 x 1.25); A = pi r^2. A frame's goal visibility is w = its green-mask pixel count / A, and its green centroid is the mean (row, column) of its green-mask pixels (the green mask as protocol-1's), both unrounded. rho(f) is the largest distance, in units of the radius, from a disc's centre to the centroid of a region covering a fraction f of it, which is the circular segment of that area: rho(f) = 4 sin^3(theta / 2) / (3 (theta - sin theta)) with (theta - sin theta) / (2 pi) = f for 0 < f < 1, and rho(f) = 0 for f >= 1. A frame's goal envelope is rho(min(w, 1)) x r + 1.5 px. In-sample r ran from 11.5 to 13.9 px.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part, every check applied to every candidate: manifest: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; frame_shape: every frame has the render's shape; first_frame: frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; cube_size: in every size-checkable frame, r is within the pilot-set size band [a_lo, a_hi], subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56 (protocol-2's size check, unchanged); cube_presence: the final frame T shows the cube (r >= 0.02), and a final frame that shows no cube or whose visibility is uncertain fails; extra_red: in every frame, no red component outside the merge radius has at least 0.25 x the snapshot render's cube area; goal_envelope: in every frame with at least one green pixel, the green pixels' centroid is within that frame's goal envelope of p (goal_geometry); goal_final: the final frame T has goal visibility w >= 0.4, and a final frame with w < 0.4, including one with no green pixel, fails. There is no per-frame cube presence requirement and no upper area bound outside the size-checkable frames; the goal check has no visibility cut and no pilot-set tolerance. A snapshot render with no cube fails cube_size and cube_presence; a snapshot render with no green pixel fails goal_envelope and goal_final. A candidate with no size-checkable frame (n = 0) gets no cube_size check and still gets cube_presence. For T = 15 planning-failure episodes every frame is size-checkable, so frame T meets both rules.
ET-M3-1.how_it_tells_missing_from_occluded: No single frame tells a hidden cube from a missing one: a cube held or covered by the gripper can show no pixels at all (in-sample, 40 frames in one episode). So the rule uses when a frame comes, not what it shows. (1) Before the arm is first commanded near the camera-to-cube sightline, nothing can hide the cube, so cube_size requires the whole cube at its size; a missing or uncertain cube there fails. (2) After that, the checker accepts a frame that shows no cube or is uncertain, without deciding which; a missing cube and an occluded one are treated alike there. (3) At the final frame the cube must be seen again (r >= 0.02). Uncertain visibility at T counts as not seen and fails: the checker needs positive evidence that the cube still exists at the end. The cost: a candidate whose cube is legitimately hidden at its last frame, or knocked off the table or out of view, is rejected, which the checker cannot tell from removal. 'Shows the cube' is only a red area of at least 0.02 x the reference; it does not check position or shape after the size-checkable frames.
ET-M3-1.how_the_goal_check_tells_occlusion_from_: (1) The reference is the goal's projected centre and size from the frozen manifest, not the snapshot render, whose goal can itself be partly hidden. (2) An occluder removes part of the goal's disc and nothing else, so the centroid of what stays visible lies within rho(w) r of p whatever the occluder's shape; the envelope allows exactly that, plus 1.5 px for mask edges and shading. A moved goal carries its whole visible region with it, so a 0.03 m move (at least 11.35 px in-sample) puts the centroid outside the envelope once enough of the goal shows: certainly when the whole-pixel move exceeds 2 rho(w) r + 1.5 px (on every in-sample scene once w >= 0.53, or w >= 0.58 allowing the largest observed 0.89 px excess), and in-sample in every frame with w >= 0.5. (3) When most of the goal is hidden the envelope widens toward r + 1.5 px, and a moved goal cannot be told from a hidden one: such frames are still checked, but only a larger move is caught there. (4) When every frame after a goal change is poorly visible: there is no eligibility cut, so every frame with any green pixel is checked against its own envelope, and goal_final requires the final frame to show at least 40% of the goal's disc. A goal change that lasts to the end is therefore judged at frame T with an envelope of at most rho(0.4) r + 1.5 = 0.511 r + 1.5 px, and hiding the goal at T (w < 0.4, or no green) fails goal_final outright. Making the goal harder to see cannot let a lasting change pass unjudged: either the goal is seen well enough at T, or the candidate is rejected. The cost: a candidate whose goal is legitimately more than 60% covered at its last frame is rejected, which the checker cannot tell from a removed goal. A goal change that is undone before T, and is poorly visible while it lasts, is not caught (limits).
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10940 to 10959, used for nothing else, with the episode_kind alternation. The masks (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity) and the rule are protocol-1's: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10% (upper extremes x 1.1, lower x 0.9). The size band takes r's extremes over size-checkable frames only, subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56; the merge radius and first-frame tolerance are taken over every frame. No presence band is set, and nothing of the goal check is pilot-set: the 1.5 px margin and the 0.4 floor are fixed here. The pilot records each candidate's n, and at every frame the simulator's cube position, the sightline clearance of the simulator's actual joint positions, and the goal's w, the distance of the green centroid from p, and the envelope. It evaluates every condition below and, if any holds, writes nothing to evals/, lists all that hold, and the owner is told before any control or injection is generated: (1) more than 2 of the 20 pilot candidates have no size-checkable frame t with 1 <= t <= T - 1; (2) in a size-checkable pilot frame the simulator's cube centre is more than 0.005 m from its initial position; (3) a size-checkable pilot frame's r is outside [0.95, 1.05]; (4) the widened size band is not inside its limits; (5) no pilot frame is size-checkable; (6) a snapshot render shows no cube or no goal; (7) a pilot candidate's final frame does not show the cube (r < 0.02); (8) the merge radius is 60 px or more, the smallest duplicate offset, so a duplicate could merge with the cube; (9) a pilot frame with at least one green pixel has its green centroid outside its goal envelope, or a pilot candidate's final frame has w < 0.4, so an unmodified candidate would fail the goal check; (10) on some pilot candidate's final frame, for some direction every 1 degree in xy, the whole-pixel image shift that a type-4 goal-pixel injection applies for a 0.03 m goal move (inject.goal_pixel_shift, rounded half up), added to that frame's green centroid, stays within the frame's goal envelope of p, so such an injection could pass at frame T. A snapshot without an exposed render camera refuses the run, before any result is written. Otherwise the tolerances go to evals/M3-checker-tolerances-p4.json with protocol_version m3-protocol-4, and its sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated.

ET-M3-1.threshold: 100% of the 60 injected candidates rejected, an injection counting as rejected only when its unmodified source candidate passes every check and the injected one fails at least one (an injection whose source fails, or that is not built, counts as not rejected); and at most 3 of the 60 controls (5%) falsely rejected
ET-M3-1.if_it_fails: recorded as failed. A further revision needs m3-protocol-5, the owner's decision, a new tolerance pilot on unused block 10 seeds, and fresh controls and injections on new seeds
ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; how often the size check runs (protocol-2's list); for every candidate its final-frame r, its longest run of frames with r < 0.02 and where it starts, and, from the simulator, its final cube position and whether that is on the table and projects inside the image (reporting only, not part of the rule); the number of candidates whose final frame is uncertain or shows no cube; the pilot's merge radius against stop (8), and its largest goal-centroid excess over the envelope, smallest final-frame w and smallest final-frame margin of a 0.03 m shift beyond the envelope against stops (9) and (10); for every candidate its final-frame goal w and its largest goal-centroid excess over the envelope (in the run record, per frame: w, the centroid's distance from p and the envelope); for each type-4 injection its subtype, step, shift and the first frame where goal_envelope failed; each type-3 injection's seed, skipped seeds, step and T; what happens at n = 0 and when visibility is uncertain (above); the limits below; and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)
ET-M3-1.risk_before_freezing: estimated, not measured. The goal check: no in-sample frame came within 0.6 px of failing goal_envelope (largest excess 0.89 px against the 1.5 px margin), so false rejections there need occlusion or shading unlike any of 10,121 frames. goal_final is the new binding risk: the lowest in-sample final w was 0.452 and the next 0.500, so a fresh candidate below 0.4 is plausible; a rate of 1 in 300 to 1 in 100 per episode would give about 18% to 45% that at least one of 60 sources fails goal_final (one failing source fails the test), and more than 3 of 60 controls failing is unlikely (under 2%). A floor of 0.3 would lower that rate at the cost of weaker judgement of a goal change at frame T (in-sample a 0.03 m shift was caught in 255 of 364 frames with 0.3 <= w < 0.4). Protocol-3's cube_presence risk stays as estimated there (17% to 31%). Type 4's goal-pixel shift relies on goal_envelope, guarded by stop (10) on the pilot's final frames; type 2 relies on extra_red (stop 8).
ET-M3-1.limits: A cube that disappears after the size-checkable frames and reappears before the end is not caught by cube_presence, and a size error after those frames is not caught by cube_size; an enlarged cube is caught only in size-checkable frames. ET-M3-1 shows that the checker catches a removal that persists to the end, a duplicate, and a resize that starts before the arm approaches. ET-M3-2 has to judge presence and size in the frames between. For the goal: a goal change that is undone before the final frame is caught only in frames where enough of the goal shows (in-sample a 0.03 m move left the envelope in every frame with w >= 0.5, and less often below); a lasting change is judged at frame T. goal_envelope checks the position of the visible green, not the goal's size or a second green object. ET-M3-2 has to judge temporary disappearances, late resizes and poorly visible goal changes in generated trajectories.
